Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.7: Lumbar Fusion (with or without Decompression) Following Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Surgery

Required findings: Post‑operative imaging (X‑ray, CT, or MRI) demonstrates implant malposition or failure such as subsidence, loosening, infection, dislocation, subluxation, vertebral body fracture, or dislodgement
Clinical documentation confirming the implant has failed and correlates with patient symptoms
No additional time‑based requirement beyond documentation of failure
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Failed Lumbar Disc Arthroplasty Implant

Required findings: At least six (6) months have elapsed since the prior lumbar total disc arthroplasty at the same level
Post‑operative MRI or CT demonstrates compression of neural structures (e.g., retained disc material or recurrent disc herniation)
Patient meets all criteria in the applicable procedure‑specific section (CMM-609.4 Lumbar Fusion with Decompression or CMM-609.5 Lumbar Fusion without Decompression)
Clinical symptoms consistent with neural compression (e.g., radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication) documented in the medical record
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.7 > Evidence of Neural Structure Compression

Non-Indications: Less than six months have passed since the original lumbar disc arthroplasty at the same level
Absence of imaging evidence of implant malposition/failure or neural structure compression
Failure to satisfy the criteria outlined in the applicable procedure‑specific sections (CMM-609.4 or CMM-609.5)
Patient does not exhibit clinical symptoms attributable to neural compression
Important criteria & exceptions: Procedure must be performed at a level where the prior disc arthroplasty was placed
For neural compression indication, the case must also satisfy all requirements of either CMM‑609.4 (fusion with decompression) or CMM‑609.5 (fusion without decompression)
The six‑month post‑arthroplasty interval is mandatory; earlier surgery is not covered
Documentation required: Operative report of the original lumbar total disc arthroplasty
Post‑operative imaging report (X‑ray, CT, or MRI) showing implant malposition, subsidence, loosening, infection, dislocation, subluxation, fracture, or dislodgement
Post‑operative MRI or CT report demonstrating neural structure compression (retained disc material or recurrent herniation)
Clinical notes documenting symptom onset, severity, and functional impairment consistent with neural compression
Date of prior arthroplasty to verify the ≥6‑month interval
Documentation that the patient meets all criteria in the relevant procedure‑specific section (CMM‑609.4 or CMM‑609.5)
